newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore Power opens $240 million gas plant.
newsitem.headline: Singapore Power opens $240 million gas plant.

text.p: State power monopoly Singapore Power opened a new Singapore $240 million gas production plant on Friday, which will help meet the island's growing demand for piped gas, Minister for Trade and Industry Lee Yock Suan said.
"Demand for piped gas has been increasing rapidly, at an average of some six percent per annum, over the last five years," he said in a speech to mark the opening.
"The daily peak demand (in Singapore) for gas has crossed the 700,000 cubic metres mark, compared to 450,000 cubic metres in 1990," Lee said, referring to residential demand.
The Senoko Gasworks in the north of the island, has a daily production capacity of 1.6 million cubic metres.
Its production capacity is 45 percent greater than the company's existing plant in central Singapore, Singapore Power Chairman, Ho Kwon Ping, said.
"Storage capacity has also increased by six-fold to 300,000 cubic metres, thereby further enhancing the reliability of supply," he said.

"To bring gas from the new Senoko Gas works to the existing network and to expand the reach of piped gas, a 70-km pipeline linking the gasworks to the existing network has also been constructed at a cost of $100 million," Ho said.
Lee said the ministry was conducting a feasibililty study to import natural gas from its neighbours, including the giant Natuna gas field offshore Indonesia.
Wong Toon Suan, managing director of Power Gas, said the firm was expecting a turnover of Singapore $130-$140 million in its financial year to the end of March 1997.
